purpose: Behavioral evaluation cases for ShipGuard scoring and launch decisions.

cases.description: A privileged Supabase service-role key is committed in a tracked environment file.
evidence: Repository contains a tracked .env.production file.
The file includes SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY with a non-placeholder value.

cases.description: A user-facing data query lacks tenant scoping and allows authenticated users to read another tenant's records.
evidence: The route accepts an arbitrary tenantId from the request.
Authorization checks only verify that the requester is authenticated.
The database query filters by the supplied tenantId without verifying tenant membership.

cases.description: A public password-reset or login endpoint has no visible abuse protection.
evidence: The public authentication endpoint is present.
No application-level rate limiter is present in the inspected request path.
Upstream platform rate limiting cannot be verified.

expected.notes: Do not claim there is definitively no rate limiting when upstream infrastructure was not inspected.

cases.description: A high-volume lookup filters on an unindexed foreign key.
evidence: Query path repeatedly filters orders by customer_id.
Schema and migrations show no index covering customer_id.

cases.description: The application cannot produce a production build due to a deterministic TypeScript error.
evidence: Production build command exits non-zero.
The failure is reproducible and occurs before an artifact is created.

cases.description: No monitoring configuration is visible in the repository, but deployment-platform settings were not provided.
evidence: No repository-level monitoring SDK or config is found.
Production platform configuration is unavailable.

expected.notes: Report as a verification gap rather than asserting that monitoring does not exist.

cases.description: A production-ready application has verified authorization, safe secrets handling, successful build, migrations, monitoring, and rollback controls.
evidence: Production build succeeds.
Secrets are injected by the deployment platform and no real credentials are committed.
Authorization is enforced server-side on protected operations.
Tenant-scoped database policies are present and tested.
Error monitoring and health checks are configured.
Deployment procedure includes tested rollback guidance.

cases.description: An otherwise mature application has one confirmed authorization bypass.
evidence: Most production controls are verified and would produce a score above 90 before blocker evaluation.
One admin mutation route trusts a client-supplied role and performs no server-side authorization check.

expected.notes: The launch decision must override the raw numeric score.
